purpose: Resolves a vendor model string to its API name, family, generation, and strength. Data rather than code so a vendor's new model name does not require a release. A name absent from here is recorded unresolved, never guessed: the harness label is retained verbatim in every case, and only the derived fields are left null.
matching: Case-folded exact match on the whole string. Not a substring or prefix match -- 'claude' appears inside Cursor's model names as well as Anthropic's, so a token match cannot tell provider from family.

<synthetic>.meaning: Claude's own placeholder where no model answered; observed on 62 real records. Recorded as a sentinel rather than parsed, so it never yields a family or generation.

default.meaning: Cursor records the absence of an explicit model choice. Different from an unknown model, and not resolvable to one.

dimensions.strength: Reasoning effort a user selected: high, medium, low. Independent of speed. A model offering only one level states it the same way as one where it was chosen, so a recorded strength does not by itself prove the user picked it.
dimensions.speed: A separate dimension, filled only when the vendor names it. Only `fast` is ever stated across the observed corpus -- there is no `slow` or `standard` token -- so an absent speed means not stated rather than standard, and the column stays null.
dimensions.note: One label can state both: cursor-grok-4.5-high-fast is a high strength at a fast speed.

axes.line: The vendor's model line: claude, gpt, grok, composer. Names the series, not one model.
axes.generation: The major step of a line, counted in whole numbers. Claude has gone 3, 4, 5; GPT likewise 3, 4, 5. A generation is a family of models, not a single one.
axes.version: The release within a generation: GPT 5.6 and Claude 4.8 are versions of generations 5 and 4. Recorded whole, so generation is recoverable from it but never conflated with it.
axes.gradation: The capability level within a version. Anthropic names these after a mythology and a form -- opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, mythos; OpenAI names them for a purpose -- codex, sol, terra. The axis is the same one, and 'thinking' or 'coding' in other vendors' names occupies it too.
axes.strength: Reasoning effort selected: high, medium, low. Independent of gradation and of speed. A model offering only one level states it the same way as one where it was chosen, so a recorded strength does not prove the user picked it.
axes.speed: A separate dimension, filled only when the vendor names it. Only `fast` is ever stated across the observed corpus -- there is no `slow` or `standard` -- so an absent speed means not stated rather than standard.

gradations.note: The capability level within one version, listed from lowest to highest. Anthropic names these after literary and mythological forms, OpenAI after celestial bodies; other vendors write `thinking` or `coding` in the same slot. Mythos is named and not generally available. The order is the vendor's own ranking and is recorded because it is not recoverable from the names.

variants.note: Superseded or purpose-marking designators a vendor has used in the gradation position at other times. Kept distinct from gradation so a historical `codex` is not read as a current capability level.

derivation.order: Alias table first, then the per-vendor tokenizer, then unresolved. `basis` on each result records which path produced it, so a curated mapping is distinguishable from a parsed one.
derivation.api_names: An `api` value is the identifier the provider recognizes, stated explicitly here rather than inferred at read time. Correcting one is a data edit.
